title: The gathering
hookLine: all people gathered on one plain

lines: A LAND LIKE A LOAF OF FINE FLOUR.
cards: No skyline. No street signs. No tree to meet under, no house to point at, no hill to climb for a better view.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari describes the ground of the Day of Resurrection like that: a white land, tinged with red, like a round loaf of fine flour, with no landmark on it belonging to anyone.
Flat, open, and nobody's property. On that plain, the Qur'an says, every person will stand.

teach.b: The Arabic is al-hashr, the gathering, and the Day is sometimes called yawm al-hashr. Surah al-Kahf says Allah will gather them and leave not one of them behind. Not one.
And notice what's missing on that plain. In this life people gather by something: a city, a team, a language, a family name, a mosque, a church. Here, the hadith says, there's no landmark for anyone.
No one's corner, no one's side of town. The Qur'an adds that each will come alone, as they were first created. Another hadith in Bukhari makes it even plainer.

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said people will be gathered barefoot, unclothed, as they were born. 'A'ishah, his wife, heard it and asked the obvious question: men and women, looking at one another?

teach.h: TOO SERIOUS TO CARE ABOUT THAT.
teach.b: And he answered, in paraphrase: the matter will be too serious for them to care about that. Everything people usually notice about each other, clothes, status, looks, is gone, and so is the urge to notice it.
What's left is a person, and what they did.

So the gathering is two things at once: a crowd with no one missing, all together on one plain, and each person in it standing alone, coming as they were made. The next days of this part follow what happens on that plain.

how: Muslims believe all people will be raised and gathered for judgment on the Day of Resurrection; teachers sometimes point to the crowds of the Hajj at Arafat, all in plain white, as a reminder of that gathering.

o: everyone raised and brought together on one plain, none left behind
Friday's weekly congregation for prayer at the mosque
the yearly crowd of pilgrims standing together at Arafah

p: leave not one of them behind
like a loaf of fine flour
men and women, looking at one another?

s: the hadith says people on the plain will gather by city and family
it says there will be no landmark for anyone.
'A'ishah asked about men and women seeing one another, and was told it would be too serious to care
al-Kahf says some people will be left behind
it says Allah will gather them and leave not one of them behind.

games.q: you're 'A'ishah. you've just heard people will be gathered unclothed, as they were born. what do you do?
o: stay quiet and hope you misheard.
ask: men and women, looking at one another?
games.why: she asked the obvious question, and the answer was that the matter would be too serious for anyone to care about that.

practice: Picture a wide, flat, pale plain, and set on it the people closest to you, then the people you saw today, the stranger in line, the neighbor, then people from far away and from history, even people you've argued with, until it's full, with no landmarks and no sides.
Stand among them and notice that nothing marks you out. If you pray, you can ask for mercy for all of them, in whatever words your tradition uses; if not, simply look at the crowd with kindness.

wordCard.voice: The gathering. Al-hashr: everyone raised and brought together on one plain on the Day of Resurrection, leaving not one behind. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the gathering; yawm al-hashr, the Day of Gathering.

carryVoice: Your line: all together. A crowd with no one missing, and no one's corner. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Qur'an 18:47 (We gather them and leave not one behind)
Qur'an 6:94 (you come to Us alone, as We created you at first)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6521 (Sahl ibn Sa'd: a white, reddish land like a loaf of fine flour, with no landmark)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6527 ('A'ishah: gathered barefoot and unclothed)
